Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. I pulled together baseline hosted API pricing and a short MAP; attaching both. High level answers below (short version so procurement has something to review quickly):

1) Baseline pricing (hosted embeddings) — per-vector (unit) model
- 256-d: $0.00045 per vector
- 512-d: $0.00075 per vector
- 768-d: $0.00105 per vector
- 1536-d: $0.00190 per vector

Note: we price per returned embedding vector. For multi-vector responses (batch API) the server aggregates vectors and charges sum of units. We also offer a per-1M-vector bundle for volume customers (see attached ratecard spreadsheet).

2) Dimensional multipliers / caps
- We treat 1–768 as base tiers above; 1536 uses a 1.8x multiplier relative to 768 (reflected in the table). Very high-d (>2048) is supported but requires enterprise packaging and potential service-level adjustments.

3) Model support
- Hosted: redwood/embedding-x-lg, open-embed-768, and quantized variants (q-embed-384) are eligible for the baseline rates.
- Proprietary or premium third-party models (licensed vendor models) may carry a model surcharge — weve flagged any such models in the attached catalog.

4) Quantized models
- Quantized/low-precision options (e.g., q-embed-384) are supported and typically priced at the same per-vector unit as comparable dimensional tiers; however, they occasionally have availability constraints at very high concurrency.

5) Discounts / committed volume
- We can offer a tiered committed-discount matrix. For a 12-month committed volume at ~200M vectors/month we would propose: 12% off baseline for a 12-month MCR starting at 100M vectors/month, plus an additional 3% rebate for annual prepayment.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) pricing looks more competitive for sustained high-throughput workloads; we can run a model to show comparative unit economics.

Attachments: Stratify-embedding-ratecard-2027-03.pdf (one-pager) and STRAT-MAP-2027-03.docx (proposed mutual action plan).

Next steps:
- Do you want a short call to walk procurement through the ratecard (I can include Karthik to explain Dedicated economics)?
- If procurement sends legal redlines or a requirements checklist we can loop Aditya for SOC/compliance notes.

Short ask from you: confirm whether the 768-d volume estimate (200M/mo) is likely all in a single region (US) and whether Stratify prefers an annual prepaid vs monthly invoicing — that affects the discount banding.

Alex / Jasmine —

Looping in with answers and a suggested path forward from the Dedicated/Private economics side. Short answers first, then a proposed next step: 

1) Billing granularity
- Hosted API: charged per returned vector unit. No per-call minimums; we bill exact units consumed per request. Bundles (per-1M vector discounts) are applied at invoice reconciliation for committed customers.

2) 1536-d handling
- 1536-d vectors are treated as higher-cost units (were already using the 1.8x multiplier Jasmine referenced). Concurrency controls are per-tenant and we reserve headroom for mixed-dimension workloads for Dedicated customers. For hosted accounts, extremely large concurrent 1536 batches may be rate-limited to protect latency SLOs — we can document typical throughput numbers in the Dedicated sizing worksheet.

3) Private/VPC pricing
- Private (VPC) pricing is a separate licensing line: it includes a platform fee plus per-vector unit rates. For large-volume customers we typically fold Private into a blended committed rate instead of the pure hosted published rates. Ive added a simple example in the attached MAP (section 3).

4) Blended committed-rate options
- We do offer blended-rate constructs for committed volumes. Typical structure: define an aggregate committed vector count (all dims normalized to 768-equivalent units), then apply a blended $/vector. This reduces billing complexity for customers who use mixed dims.

Proposed next step: 30-minute procurement sync to walk the invoice examples and a short Dedicated sizing worksheet. Jasmine — can you propose 2x 30-minute slots this week? Alex — let me know procurements preferred cadence.

Thanks,
